P0700.d: P0700 is a notice code: the separate transmission control module has stored an emission-related fault of its own and asks the engine module to switch on the check engine light. The actual fault – a sensor, solenoid, ratio or speed sensor code – is stored in the transmission module and must be read with a tool that can address it; simple OBD readers often show only P0700.
s: Check engine light, possibly transmission warning
Depending on the transmission fault: limp mode, harsh or delayed shifts
Often no symptoms if the fault was intermittent
Simple OBD reader shows only P0700
c: Actual fault stored in the transmission module (sensor, solenoid, ratio, speed sensor)
Wrong transmission fluid level or condition causing slip or ratio codes
Harness or connector at the transmission corroded or damaged
Low system voltage or weak battery

P0701.d: P0701 means the transmission control system works outside its expected range or its function is implausible – without a circuit fault. What exactly is checked is up to the manufacturer; no GM, Ford, Saab or bulletin document available to us describes the strategy.
s: Transmission warning (at Ford no check engine light)
Limp mode with fixed gear or missing gears
Harsh or irregular shifts
c: Transmission control faulty internally or software
Implausible input signals (speed or range sensor) without own circuit fault
Wrong fluid level or quality – hydraulics do not respond
Harness or connector with contact resistance

P0702.d: P0702 reports an electrical fault in the transmission control system as a whole – typically the supply of the transmission actuators (solenoid supply, transmission relay, supply switch in the module) or a circuit fault not assigned to a single component. No manufacturer document available to us describes it in detail; Ford's engine module list for 6.8 L E- and F-Series trucks stores it without the check engine light.
s: Transmission limp mode with fixed gear
Transmission warning; check engine light depending on the maker
No or harsh shifts, further solenoid codes
c: Transmission actuator supply interrupted (fuse, relay, ground)
Harness or connector at transmission or module damaged, corroded or oil-soaked
Transmission module output stage or supply switch faulty

P0703.d: Brake switch A is usually the brake light switch, B a second, redundant contact or signal used to cancel cruise control, release the converter clutch, check 'brake before throttle' and for stop-start. Since about 2014 GM receives it as a CAN message from the body module and checks its integrity (rolling counter, protection value: 3 of 10 faulty in 2014, 9 of 17 in 2025) without the check engine light; cruise control
s: Cruise control cannot be engaged or drops out
Brake light stays on or does not work
Selector cannot be moved out of P (shift lock)
Check engine light depending on the maker
c: Brake light or double switch worn, corroded or misadjusted
Wiring or connector at the pedal damaged, fuse blown
CAN message from the body module disturbed (GM: software, bus fault)
Aftermarket LED lamps or trailer module distorting the circuit

P0704.d: Only on cars with a clutch pedal: the clutch switch tells the engine module that the clutch is depressed, used to cancel cruise control, smooth load changes when shifting and for stop-start. The check is a plausibility test over driving events rather than a voltage check: Saab's Trionic T8 expects a change of state every time the car pulls away from 3 to 50 km/h (four misses in a row), the EDC16 diesel at gear change
s: Cruise control not working or not cancelling when declutching
Jerks or rev hang when shifting
Stop-start inactive
Usually no check engine light
c: Clutch switch faulty or misadjusted (does not switch or too late)
Connector or wiring at the pedal box damaged or corroded
Floor mat or pedal stop shifted, switch bracket broken
Driving style (pulling away or shifting without fully depressing the clutch)

P0710.d: The transmission fluid temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor whose resistance falls as the fluid warms; the module feeds it with 5 V through a resistor. A low signal therefore means very hot or a short to ground, a high signal very cold or an open circuit.

Torque converter clutch applies late or not at all
Check engine or transmission lamp depending on manufacturer
Implausible fluid temperature in the scan tool

P0711.d: P0711 means the fluid temperature signal is electrically valid but implausible. Torque converter clutch applies late or not at all
Check engine or transmission lamp depending on manufacturer
Implausible fluid temperature in the scan tool
c: Fluid temperature sensor drifting or stuck
High contact resistance in connector or harness (oil, corrosion)
Very cold weather or short trips (fluid does not reach warm-up threshold)
